lede: No rim and no change to either cage. The Scout's bottom opening is just the Overseer's middle rectangle (146 x 209 between node centres). Ramps rise into the opening: two shared side ramps under the long sides, two Overseer end ramps under its trapezoid tips, and two Scout end ramps under the Scout's short ends, split around the Overseer's cartridge and kept 8 mm low so the Overseer passes over them. Both cartridges seat 3 mm above the ring, so one head stop. Landing tolerance as the cages are today: Scout +-5 mm, Overseer +-10 mm.
notes: Ramp heights (mm above the seat; along its axis a 45 deg ramp catches about its own height): side 7, Overseer ends 30, Scout ends 8. The side ramps are two pads a side (x +-12..55) so they miss the corner nodes and the Scout's mid node; the Overseer end ramps sit between its tip nodes (y +-25); the Scout end ramps are pads at |y| 54..88, beside the Overseer's receiver and its TPU feet.

What limits the Overseer sideways: its belly sled and the down camera / flow pods reach y +-72 at 9 mm above the ring, right over the side ramps. With the pods pulled in to |y| 46 the side ramps can be 26 tall: Overseer +-25 mm, Scout +-10 mm (table).

Scout: its cage ends in the rectangle ring (6 mm tubes, nodes at the 4 corners and the 4 mid sides), cartridge 3 mm above the ring as the Overseer's, pack 1.0 under the FC, two latch rails for the receiver box. Overseer: cage v3 unchanged.

Box: the 6 ramps stand on a deck round the swap column (both cartridges drop straight through between them). The funnel panels and hook latch v2 retire; the hold (a latch over a ring tube) and keep-alive (pins against pads on the ring) move to the ramp bases.

Still open (concept review 27 Oct): the ring tubes slide on the ramps, so the slopes need a low-friction face (PTFE, mu <= 0.2) and the drop sim with tilt and drift before anything is printed; the 45 deg slope and these heights are concept numbers.
